title: 16-bit style pixel art background
author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
selftext: Trying to make backgrounds with retro diffusion. Aiming for backgrounds looking somewhat similar to Super Mario World. Not getting good results. Anybody got some pointers for me? Maybe my prompts are bad? Maybe retro diffusion isn’t good at this. Just surprised I can get good animations with ai but struggling with static background layers.

comments.author: nebetsu
comments.body: I would suggest generating individual assets like clouds, trees, etc and then building the background using those assets

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: Thank you. Still struggling with this. I’m really struggling with making tilesets as well lol. Tried making them the old fashion way. Tried generating some and modifying. Not getting good results. Pixel art is damn hard! For me at least.

replies.author: nebetsu
replies.body: Try studying Super Mario World backgrounds when you play it. Notice that they don't have whole backgrounds saved in the ROM. They have clouds, trees, and other background elements as reusable sprites that they invoke in the background layer of each level. If you get a feel for how they do it, it would make the background feel more legitimate for your game when you go to make backgrounds

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
Thank you. I have been doing that actually. Figured it was one big layer. Very new to this so sorry. 

I think I picked a terrible setting for a first game, which is a shopping mall. So hard to convey in pixel art. May just have to change the setting, which then I have to change story but whatever.

replies.author: nebetsu
replies.body: Retro Diffusion has a Discord. Might be worth checking out to hone your technique
